interface.signature: def minInsAndDel(N: int, M: int, A: list[int], B: list[int]) -> int:

preconditions.description: Both array lengths N and M are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= 10**5 for x in A) and all(1 <= x <= 10**5 for x in B)
preconditions.description: All elements in A and B are within the specified value bounds.
The lengths of A and B match the given N and M.
All elements in B are distinct.
Array B is sorted in non-decreasing order.

postconditions.description: The result is the sum of deletions (N - length of longest common subsequence) and insertions (M - length of longest common subsequence) required to make A identical to B.

postconditions.expression: longest_common_subsequence == max(len(lcs) for lcs in _all_possible_lcs(A, B))
postconditions.description: The longest common subsequence (LCS) between A and B is computed, where LCS is the longest sequence of elements appearing in the same order in both A and B.
